recentItems.title: Bet on Yourself: The Courage to Create Your Own Breakthrough | Priyanka Anand | TEDxHauz Khas
recentItems.description:
What if I told you the biggest bet you take in life is – betting on yourself !

In this deeply personal and powerfully inspiring talk, Priyanka Anand, Vice President and Head of HR for Ericsson Southeast Asia, Oceania, and India region, reveals the true meaning of betting on yourself — in life, in leadership, and in moments of uncertainty.

From leading large-scale corporate transformations while balancing personal loss, to redefining HR’s role in business growth and building courageous teams across borders, Priyanka shares three powerful lessons:

Lesson 1: Take a Bet on Yourself — Even when you feel unsure.
Lesson 2: Courage Creates Opportunities — Its about showing up consistently.
Lesson 3: Opportunity Needs Allies — Build your network of allies

This talk is for anyone who’s ever questioned their own readiness, their worth and were hesitant to take that one decision that could potentially change their life .

“You don’t need to be ready. You only need to be willing.”

Watch till the end — and ask yourself, are you ready to take that bet? Priyanka Anand is the Vice President and Head HR, Southeast Asia, Oceania & India at Ericsson since January 2018. An accomplished HR professional with a career spanning 20+ years, she brings a wealth of knowledge and experience. Priyanka is a transformative leader with astute business acumen and strategic mindset. Turning talent management into an instrument to drive business transformation and strategy has been her key focus area alongside developing able leaders & transforming organizational culture. In her current role, Priyanka leads a team of 60+ resources across more than 10 countries, driving HR strategy across the geography with 25k+ employees. She collaborates with Business Leaders in developing and implementing benchmark HR practices. 
Before her current role, Priyanka was Vice President and Head of HR at Ericsson Global Services, where she was pivotal in growing the organization from inception to an employee base of 15k+. She holds a management degree in Human Resources. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: AI: Altered Identity — Are We Still Thinking for Ourselves?  | TE Aravind | TEDxHauz Khas
recentItems.description:
What if the greatest risk of the AI age is not that machines become more intelligent, but that humans slowly lose sight of who they are?
In this talk, Aravind T.E. explores how the way we form beliefs has evolved from the shared worlds of radio, television and newspapers to highly personalised algorithmic feeds and, now, generative AI.
Drawing from personal experience, more than two decades of working with complex systems, and his perspective as an author, Aravind examines how repeated narratives can influence our memories, beliefs, fears, choices and ultimately our identity.
As AI becomes increasingly woven into how we search, write, decide and think, the challenge is no longer simply learning how to use artificial intelligence. It is learning how to preserve our own.
Aravind introduces the idea of *KYI — Know Your Identity*: a personal discipline of questioning what we believe, where those beliefs came from, and how much of our thinking we have unconsciously outsourced.
The future should not be a choice between human intelligence and artificial intelligence. It should be about using AI while protecting something far more fundamental: our *Authentic Intelligence*. Aravind T.E. is a banking transformation leader, published author and systems thinker with more than two decades of experience across data, tax, regulatory change and technology. Based in Singapore, he has led large-scale transformation initiatives across markets while exploring how technology reshapes human behaviour, judgment and identity. He is the author of The Memory Paradox and The Grave Cafe, works that blend psychology, technology and storytelling. His interests sit at the intersection of artificial intelligence, decision-making, systems and society. Through his writing and speaking, Aravind examines how we can embrace technological progress without surrendering independent thought, identity or human agency. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Why We Need to Stop Performing for Others | Tanay Tulsaney | TEDxHauz Khas

In this candid talk, healthcare digital strategist and podcast host Tanay Tulsaney breaks down the silent fatigue caused by modern status culture and perpetual performance, offering a fresh perspective on stripping away the filters to embrace quiet authenticity. Tanay Tulsaney is a healthcare consultant, digital media strategist, and podcast host. With extensive experience in media strategy and brand development, he focuses on the intersection of human psychology, digital communication, and authentic leadership. recentItems.title: Said “I’m Fine” Until I Wasn’t , Healing from Hidden Pain  | Shikha Yadav | TEDxHauz Khas
recentItems.description:
Sometimes the strongest smile can hide the deepest pain.

In this deeply personal talk, Shikha shares her experience of carrying grief, responsibilities, family expectations, and emotional pain while continuing to tell everyone, “I’m fine.”

Through her own healing journey, she reflects on how meditation, writing, gratitude, prayer, spirituality, and honest self-reflection helped her reconnect with herself and understand a powerful truth: healing begins when we stop pretending and allow ourselves to be seen, heard, and supported.

 This talk explores: 

- Hidden emotional struggles behind a smile
- Grief, loneliness, and emotional healing
- Why saying “I’m fine” can sometimes hide the truth
- The importance of listening without judgment
- Self-awareness and reconnecting with yourself
- Meditation, gratitude, spirituality, and writing
- Asking for help without feeling weak
- Understanding real happiness

 The power of asking someone, “How are you, really?” 


Her journey eventually led to the creation of Shikha’s Happy Land, a space built to help people pause, reconnect with themselves, and learn the art of living happily one step at a time.

This talk is a reminder that someone can appear strong, responsible, and happy while silently struggling inside.

So today, reach out to someone you care about and ask:

 “How are you, really?” 

Sometimes, your presence can mean more than your advice.

 Shikha Yadav is a dedicated Happiness and Well-being consultant and the visionary founder of Shikha’s Happyland, a platform committed to helping individuals, parents, and teenagers navigate emotional challenges with resilience and joy. Her philosophy is uniquely grounded in the timeless spiritual wisdom of the Bhagavad Gita, which she translates into practical, modern strategies for rebuilding lives with purpose. As an author and emotional fitness advocate, Shikha has gained recognition for her work in empowering young people to prioritize their mental well-being and build the "emotional fitness" necessary to bounce back from life's setbacks.
With an extensive background in understanding human behavior, Shikha’s approach draws from both spiritual insights and contemporary psychological principles. Her mission is to spread smiles and inspire a "live happily no matter what" mindset, making complex ancient teachings accessible as a "recipe for a better life" for the modern generation. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: An Earth-centric space age | Dr Rajan Bedi | TEDxNorthern Quarter
recentItems.description:
Space technology isn't only about rockets or searching for extraterrestrial life. 

This talk explores how innovation from the new space age can help solve problems on Earth and create technologies that make life safer, smarter and more sustainable. Dr Rajan Bedi has worked in the global space industry for 25 years, designing and developing the technology used on-board satellites and spacecraft. In 2014, Dr. Bedi founded Spacechips to bring-to-orbit his inventions, winning Start-Up Company of the Year and High-Reliability Product of 2025, 2018, 2017 and 2016.

In 2024, Rajan won Technology Entrepreneur of the Year and in 2020, Disruptive Entrepreneur of the Year, at the Great British Entrepreneur Awards.

Rajan became fixated on space technology at the age of five while stargazing in the crystal-clear Northern-Irish skies, becoming mesmerised by the beautiful constellations. Like most children, he read every book on space from the local library and knew then he wanted to spend his life designing and building spacecraft.

Rajan also wondered if space technology could be used to help people and make our world a safer and happier home! This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Return To Yourself | R.Ay. Febri Hapsari Dipokusumo | TEDxUNS
recentItems.description: In a world that is more connected than ever, we are also more lost than ever. Overstimulated by algorithms, driven by Fear of Missing Out (FOMO), and constantly chasing borrowed identities, we forget to ask “How much of our lives do we actually choose?” In this deeply reflective talk, R.Ay. Febri Hapsari Dipokusumo invites us to pause and rediscover a wisdom that has always been within reach. Drawing from the Javanese philosophy of Mulat Sarira, the art of looking inward, she shows that mindfulness is not a new invention, but an ancient practice embedded in our culture. Through personal stories, meditation, and the transformative power of Book Therapy, she guides us back to the self that never truly disappeared. This talk is a gentle yet powerful reminder that the greatest search in life is not to find yourself, but to know yourself. And sometimes, the answer is simply to stop, breathe, and return. RAy. Febri Hapsari Dipokusumo is a founder of FHD Motivation who focuses on nurturing inner beauty and character through the integration of traditional Javanese values and modern personal development. She dedicatedly promotes a philosophy of self-readiness that feels like a grounding anchor, blending the wisdom of the Surakarta Royal Family with contemporary social activism. As a motivator and community leader, she seeks to empower others by harmonizing ancestral heritage with the demands of the digital age, ensuring that identity remains authentic and rooted. She also has been invited as a speaker in various prestigious forums to advocate for humanitarian and social issue. Through her ideas on character training, she has touched hearts and minds, guiding the community toward a more reflective, balanced, and empowered society. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Menyadari Daya, Membentuk Makna | Wiliam Reynold | TEDxUNS
recentItems.description:
In an era defined by rapid innovation and relentless progress, there is a quieter threat unfolding among us; we are slowly becoming strangers to one another. As individualism grows, trust becomes harder to give, vulnerability feels like a weakness, and the people around us become increasingly distant despite being closer than ever. We learn to depend on ourselves, but somewhere along the way, we forget that no one was ever meant to stand alone. In TEDxUNS, William Reynolds explores Meraki, the art of pouring a piece of one’s soul into what we do and, perhaps more importantly, into the people we encounter. He reminds us that skepticism is mandatory, but trust is obligatory. To trust is not to abandon doubt, but to choose connection despite it. Because as social beings, we are shaped by the hands we hold, the people we lean on, and the relationships that remind us that we do not have to carry everything by ourselves. Perhaps, in a world that constantly teaches us to become independent, the most profound act of courage is to let someone in; to believe in one another, to rely on one another, and to leave a little piece of ourselves in the lives we touch. 

 Wiliam Reynold is the Founder of Urun Daya Kota Foundation, as well as the Executive Director of +Jakarta, a government-backed collaborative platform under DKI Jakarta Province built on the spirit of bringing people together. His journey with +Jakarta spans over four years, beginning as an Editorial member and Event Strategist before rising to lead the organization as its Executive Director, a testament to how deeply he has poured his soul into building the platform from within. He pursued a Master's degree in Urban Development Studies at the School of Strategic and Global Studies, Universitas Indonesia, and previously served as a Policy Analyst at the Governor's Delivery Unit of Jakarta City Government, where he focused on the prevention of Violence Against Women and Children as well as Urban Tourism issues, while also contributing to the early development of +Jakarta. He firmly believes that collaboration is the key to an ideal city. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Who Are You When No One Is Watching? | Kanira Jahrani Ranggadewani | TEDxUNS
recentItems.description:
In a world where achievements are constantly compared, it is easy to measure our progress against someone else’s and lose sight of our own journey. Kanira explores how comparison and the desire for validation can turn growth into a race, making us question the value of our efforts whenever we are not the one coming out on top. Through the Iceberg Illusion, she reveals the dedication, discipline, sacrifice, failure, and disappointment that often remain hidden behind visible success. She then invites us to approach our journey differently, by spending time with our own thoughts, staying in our own lane, setting small and meaningful goals, and redefining comparison as something that can either hold us back or motivate us. Rather than focusing on impressing others, she encourages us to build a sense of fulfillment that comes from within and ask a more personal question: “Who are you when no one is watching?”. 

 Kanira Jahrani Ranggadewani is the winner of TEDxUNS 5.0 Student Speaker 2026. As a first-year law student at Universitas Sebelas Maret, she continues to grow through her passion for reading, English competitions, and public speaking. Her role as Staff of International Law Development at the International Law Student Association (ILSA), along with her involvement as a staff member of BEM FH UNS Pengarusutamaan Gender, reflects her interest in inclusivity, awareness, and meaningful community discussions. Through her achievements in speech competitions, including 1st Winner of EEMC 2022, 2nd Winner of AYEC 2024, and 3rd Winner of XTENTION 2024, Kanira has developed confidence in expressing ideas and connecting with audiences. As someone who values reflection, empathy, and growth, she hopes to inspire young people to embrace their own journey beyond validation and comparison. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx

recentItems.title: Waste is only waste if we decide it is | Andrea Novita | TEDxUNS
recentItems.description: Here, TEDxUNS present to you a talk that invite us to more broadly about wastes. Andrea Novita opens her TED Talks by encouraging us to reflect that the most valuable resources can come from the little things we usually throw away. Something that belongs in a trash can hold great value and ingredients that are useful may come from the things we do not care about. Talking about waste people think about pollution, plastics, food waste, how come? Beyond waste, Andrea addresses the economy principle that drive fast-fashioned thinking. Andrea challenges that principle and guides us through her journey of creating biodegradable products from so-called waste. Andrea Novita is a content creator who focuses on rejecting environmental waste issues by translated scientific principles into visual, relatable content that educates and sparks curiosity. Andrea’s balance between exploring natural materials, applying circularity principles, and consistent public education, makes Andrea Novita’s works a meaningful representation of sustainable efforts that address current and future environmental challenges. With her background as a best graduate and got 4.00 GPA, Andrea Novita has been included in The Discover List 2026, a global recognition of 50 creators from around the world who are considered worthy of attention and have made a real impact in the Educators category. A remarkable achievements where she proved that her pure ideas will bloom in this fast paced world. This talk was given at a TEDx event using the TED conference format but independently organized by a local community. Learn more at https://www.ted.com/tedx
